claim: Convention-augmented deep reinforcement learning agents can achieve high performance with substantially fewer training steps compared to methods that do not use conventions, demonstrating improved sample efficiency in cooperative multi-agent tasks.
falsifier: In a cooperative multi-agent environment with multiple players, train a convention-augmented agent and a baseline agent without conventions, recording the number of training steps needed to reach a target performance level. Compare the step counts to assess sample efficiency.

conditions: conventions are appended to the primitive-action space
comparison is against ACHA (a multi-agent RL algorithm) that required 20 billion steps
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system, task (five-player Hanabi), population (Rainbow with conventions vs. ACHA), and experimental conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Augmentation of the action–high performance with far principle
